summary: On cooling the monolayer from 300 K to 4 K, the two Ag phonons near 237 and 338 cm-1 harden by about 5 and 3 cm-1 and narrow, and the 4 K spectrum looks like an ordinary anharmonic freeze-out. Broad extra bands also grow in near 300 cm-1 (visible by 150 K) and near 358 cm-1 (visible by 80 K), absent at 300 K. Their onset roughly tracks the expected intralayer ferromagnetic ordering (about 150 K) and the sub-100 K regime. I read them as a magnetic-order-related effect, possibly spin-phonon coupling or symmetry-lowering, and I did not assign them. Absolute intensities are not comparable between temperatures, and the data cannot tell the magnetic order type or the cause of the extra bands.

observations.finding: Both strong Ag-type modes harden and sharpen on cooling; most of the shift occurs between 300 and about 150 to 80 K, and little changes below 80 K.
observations.evidence: Single-Lorentzian fits (±1σ fit error). Low-energy Ag mode: 237.05±0.22 (300 K), 239.94±0.35 (150 K), 242.13±0.37 (80 K), 242.04±0.20 cm-1 (4 K), FWHM about 10.5, 9.6, 11.6, 6.5 cm-1. High-energy Ag mode: 338.37±0.14, 340.58±0.09, 341.37±0.19, 341.44±0.17 cm-1, FWHM 7.0, 4.9, 5.0, 4.7 cm-1. Total shift is +5.0 and +3.1 cm-1. The FWHM is not corrected for instrumental broadening, and the point spacing is 1.3 to 3.9 cm-1.

observations.finding: New broad bands appear at low temperature in the cross-circular channel. A band at about 285-320 cm-1 (peaks near 297, 302 and 312 cm-1) is clear by 150 K and strong at 80 K and 4 K. A band at about 350-365 cm-1 (peak 357-358 cm-1) is absent at 150 K and clear at 80 K and 4 K. Neither is distinguishable from noise at 300 K.
observations.evidence: Integrated area over 285-322 cm-1 divided by the area of the 338-341 cm-1 mode: 0.08 (300 K, about 2σ, not significant), 0.31 (150 K), 0.48 (80 K), 0.55 (4 K); absolute area 100±46, 202±22, 218±18, 807±45 counts·cm-1. Area over 348-372 cm-1 divided by the 338-341 cm-1 area: 0.03 (300 K), 0.05 (150 K), 0.41 (80 K), 0.41 (4 K); absolute 35±37, 31±18, 186±14, 591±34 counts·cm-1. There is no signal above noise at 372-400 cm-1 at any temperature. The 4 K peak list shows 394 cm-1 at only about 15 counts, which I treat as noise.

observations.finding: The emergence of the extra bands is consistent with a magnetic-order-related origin, but the data do not prove it. The 300 cm-1 band already appears at about 150 K, close to the reported intralayer ferromagnetic ordering temperature of monolayer and few-layer CrSBr. The 358 cm-1 band appears later, between 150 and 80 K.
observations.evidence: The temperature dependence of band areas is set out in the previous observation; there are only four temperatures. Phonon hardening saturates below about 80 K, whereas the extra-band areas keep growing to 4 K, which is a different temperature dependence from the Ag mode shifts.
observations.source: CrSBr Tc and spin-phonon Raman work as recalled from memory (Lee et al., Nano Lett. 2021; Pawbake et al., Phys. Rev. B 107, 075421, 2023; Ergeçen et al., Nat. Commun. 2022). I did not re-check the figures, so verify before quoting.

observations.finding: The crystal quality of the monolayer is reasonable. The Ag lines are narrow at low temperature (about 4.7 cm-1 for the 341 cm-1 mode), the baseline is clean, and there is no obvious disorder broadening or extra defect modes at 300 K.
observations.evidence: At 300 K only the two Ag modes are significant, with a flat baseline (noise about 7 counts at 300 K and 4 K, about 2.5 to 3 at 80 and 150 K). The 237 cm-1 mode is broader and noisier than the 338 cm-1 one, and its FWHM is poorly constrained (6.5 to 11.6 cm-1).

observations.finding: Raw intensities do not follow a smooth trend with temperature, so they cannot be used for quantitative comparison.
observations.evidence: Peak height of the 340 cm-1 mode is about 137, 97, 70 and 207 counts at 300, 150, 80 and 4 K. This is non-monotonic, whereas the Ag2/Ag3 area ratio is 0.67, 0.55, 0.77 and 0.52. The ratio changes by less than the likely fit and noise uncertainty.

caveats: Four temperatures only, and the window starts at about 150 cm-1, so the strong Ag mode near 118 cm-1 is outside the data. The most magnetically sensitive low-energy behaviour (magnon and low-energy modes) is therefore not covered.

Heating by the laser (532 nm, 100x objective) can make the real sample temperature higher than the nominal one, especially for a monolayer on a poorly conducting substrate. The monolayer sits under the nominal value, so the onset temperatures of the extra bands may be off. The laser power is not given.

Intensities are not comparable across temperatures. Focus drift on cooling in a PPMS insert, substrate interference, and resonance changes in the optical gap (CrSBr has strong excitonic resonances near 1.3 eV and higher) all change the signal. The 340 cm-1 peak height goes 137, 97, 70, 207 counts, which is non-monotonic. Use ratios and positions, not absolute intensity.

In crossed circular detection, Ag modes with a diagonal tensor are partly suppressed or polarization-dependent. A change in which modes appear can come from polarization-selection changes (for example, optical anisotropy or sample rotation) and not only from new scattering mechanisms. The polarization was not changed during the measurement, so this cannot be separated. A linear co/cross polarization map at 4 K would help.

The 285-320 cm-1 and 350-365 cm-1 features are broad, only a few points wide, and the 4 K noise is about 6.5 counts. I did not fit them as separate peaks and did not assign them to specific modes. Candidate explanations are Bg or infrared modes made visible by symmetry lowering, two-phonon features, or magnetic-order-induced mode activation, none of which this data distinguishes.
Spectra were recorded on cooling after stabilization, so thermal hysteresis (for example, a thermally induced strain step from the substrate) cannot be excluded. A warming run would be needed.
A few points are missing in some traces. The point spacing varies between files (1.3 to 3.9 cm-1), which limits the peak-position precision of the 80 K spectrum in particular.
Literature references in this report are from memory and were not re-checked against the papers, so I cite them without figure numbers.
questions_for_user: What laser power and spot size were used, and is the sample on a thermally conducting substrate? This tells me how far the real sample temperature is above the thermometer reading.
Were the spectra taken at the same spot, with refocusing at each temperature? The intensity is non-monotonic and I need to know whether to trust any intensity ratios.
What is the substrate and capping (for example, SiO2/Si, hBN encapsulation)? This affects strain on cooling, interference, and whether the sample is protected from degradation.

Can you provide linear co/cross spectra at 4 K, and a finer temperature series between 80 and 150 K, plus a warming run? These would show whether the 300 and 358 cm-1 bands follow an order-parameter-like curve and identify their symmetry.
Do you have the low-wavenumber window below 150 cm-1 (the 118 cm-1 Ag mode)? It is the most sensitive to magnetic order and would help the assignment.

Were the magnetic properties of the monolayer characterized by another method (for example, magneto-optics or MCD)? That would let me tie the onset temperatures to a magnetic transition and not just to the Raman data.

limits: The data cannot identify the magnetic order (ferromagnetic intralayer order versus other states) or give a transition temperature. Only four temperatures were measured, and the laser heating is unknown.
The data cannot assign the 300 and 358 cm-1 bands to specific symmetries or mechanisms. A polarization-resolved or magnetic-field-dependent study is needed.

The data cannot separate strain or substrate effects from intrinsic anharmonic and spin-phonon shifts of the Ag modes. There is no reference spectrum for a strain-free sample, and no comparison to a bulk or bilayer sample.

The data cannot confirm thickness. The monolayer assignment rests on the AFM information you gave, and the Raman alone (one polarization configuration, no thickness series) does not independently confirm it.
The window starts at about 150 cm-1, so the lowest-energy Ag mode and any low-energy magnon-like features are not covered.
